definitions.gloss: matchmaking; acting as go-between for a marriage
definitions.explanation: The act of introducing a prospective bride and groom and facilitating their marriage, or presiding over the wedding ceremony as a formal witness.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}に{媒酌|ばいしゃく}を{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I asked my boss to serve as matchmaker.

examples.japanese: {媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}が{両家|りょうけ}を{引|ひ}き{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: The matchmaker introduced the two families to each other.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}を{立|た}てない{結婚式|けっこんしき}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Recently, weddings without a formal matchmaker have been increasing.

notes:
A formal term from traditional Japanese marriage customs. The {媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん} (matchmaker/go-between) was historically a respected married couple who introduced the bride and groom, helped negotiate between families, and presided over the wedding ceremony. While {見合|みあ}い (arranged marriage meetings) still occur, the formal role of {媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん} has become much less common in modern Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}: matchmaker; go-between
- {媒酌|ばいしゃく}を{務|つと}める: to serve as matchmaker
- {媒酌|ばいしゃく}を{頼|たの}む: to ask someone to be matchmaker
- {媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}を{立|た}てる: to have a formal matchmaker

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仲人|なこうど}: matchmaker; go-between — more commonly used in everyday language; largely interchangeable
- {見合|みあ}い: arranged meeting for marriage — the meeting itself, not the matchmaking role
- お{見合|みあ}い: arranged marriage meeting (polite form)
